briefs.headline: West Virginia beats Auburn 76-70 in Las Vegas to open the Players Era
briefs.summary: West Virginia led Auburn 36-31 at the half and won 76-70 at Michelob Ultra Arena in Las Vegas early Wednesday morning Eastern time, per ESPN's box score of the Players Era first-round game, which tipped at 11:59 p.m. ET Tuesday before 5,144. Brenen Lorient scored 19 points with three steals, Amadou Seini had nine rebounds and Miles Sadler six assists; West Virginia was 19 of 23 at the line to Auburn's 13 of 22 and made 7 of 22 threes. Tahaad Pettiford led Auburn with 21 points and three steals. The Mountaineers are four wins and no losses and play Kansas in the same arena on Wednesday at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2; Auburn fell to two wins and two losses.

briefs.headline: Ohio scores 21 in the fourth to beat Ball State 35-28 at Peden
briefs.summary: Ohio trailed Ball State 20-14 at the half, played a scoreless third quarter and scored 21 points in the fourth to win 35-28 at Peden Stadium in Athens on Tuesday night before 12,237, per ESPN's box score; the quarters went Ohio 7, 7, 0, 21 against Ball State 3, 17, 0, 8. The Bobcats are eight wins and three losses overall and six and one in the MAC per the box score records, and the ESPN conference table lists them second of 13 behind Toledo; Ball State is three wins and eight losses.

briefs.headline: Pulisic and Hall score as the USMNT beats Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati
briefs.summary: Christian Pulisic scored in the 25th minute and Julian Hall in the 43rd, both from Weston McKennie assists, and the United States beat Haiti 2-0 at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on Tuesday to complete an 8-0 aggregate win in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal, per ESPN's match summary; the U.S. had 74.2% of possession and 13 shots to eight. ESPN reported it was Mauricio Pochettino's final game as coach before he takes over Manchester United, and that the semifinal in March is against Jamaica or Mexico.

briefs.headline: Marshall beats East Tennessee State 67-55 for a second win
briefs.summary: Marshall led 28-17 at the half and closed out East Tennessee State 67-55 at the Cam Henderson Center in Huntington on Tuesday before 4,327, per ESPN's box score. Fazl Oshodi scored 20 points, Luke Rasmussen had 10 rebounds and Noah Otshudi seven assists; the Herd outrebounded the Buccaneers 48 to 31 and made 10 of 30 threes, while East Tennessee State was 4 of 13 at the line. The Herd's record is two and three, and the next game is at North Carolina on Friday at 9 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Pistons end the Spurs' winning streak at 12 with a 105 to 93 win in San Antonio
briefs.summary: Detroit beat San Antonio 105 to 93 at the Frost Bank Center on Tuesday before 18,412, ending the Spurs' run of 12 straight wins, per ESPN's box score; the quarters went Detroit 26, 29, 23, 27 against San Antonio 33, 21, 18, 21, the Spurs leading by seven after one and outscored in each of the last three. Victor Wembanyama had 25 points and 18 rebounds and Stephon Castle seven assists for San Antonio, which shot 22.5% from three on 40 attempts; Cade Cunningham scored 27 for Detroit and Ausar Thompson had 14 points, nine rebounds, 12 assists and five steals. The Spurs are 12 wins and three defeats and dropped to second in the West, one game behind the Lakers; the Pistons are nine wins and four defeats.

briefs.headline: Reds add first baseman Carter Graham to the 40-man roster
briefs.summary: The Reds selected the contract of first baseman Carter Graham from Triple-A Louisville on Tuesday, per the MLB Stats API transaction log for Nov. 17, read at 5:47 a.m. ET Wednesday, the only Cincinnati entry among 208 transactions logged across the league on the day clubs set their 40-man rosters ahead of the Rule 5 draft.

briefs.headline: Pirates protect catcher Axiel Plaz and outfielder Mitch Jebb
briefs.summary: The Pirates selected the contracts of catcher Axiel Plaz from High-A Greensboro and outfielder Mitch Jebb from Triple-A Indianapolis on Tuesday, per the MLB Stats API transaction log for Nov. 17, read at 5:47 a.m. ET Wednesday, Pittsburgh's two entries among 208 transactions logged across the league on the day clubs set their 40-man rosters ahead of the Rule 5 draft.

briefs.headline: Wakamotoharu leads the Kyushu basho alone at 10 wins after Kotozakura throws Atamifuji
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association's tournament leaders page lists maegashira (rank-and-file) 7 Wakamotoharu alone at 10 wins and one loss after day 11 of the Kyushu basho (tournament) in Fukuoka on Wednesday, with three rikishi (wrestlers) one behind at nine and two: yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato, sekiwake Atamifuji and maegashira 7 Kinbozan. Per the SumoDB results table for the day, Wakamotoharu beat maegashira 14 Dewanoryu with an uwatehineri (overarm twisting throw) for a ninth straight win; ozeki (champion) Kotozakura threw Atamifuji with an uwatenage (overarm throw) to end the sekiwake's share of the lead and even his own record at six and five; Onosato pushed out sekiwake Fujinokawa; Kinbozan pushed out Asahakuryu; yokozuna Hoshoryu forced out ozeki Kirishima, dropping Kirishima to eight and three and putting Hoshoryu at six and five; and maegashira 4 Takerufuji, already at a make-koshi (losing record), crushed out ozeki Aonishiki, who is six and five. Dewanoryu, Kirishima, Roga and Tamawashi are the four at eight and three. In juryo (the second division) the JSA lists Wakatakakage and Asahifuji level at 10 and one with Enho and Tamashoho at nine and two. Day 12 is Thursday; the final day is Sunday, Nov. 22.

waters.reading: 97.3 cfs, 1.62 feet at 5:15 a.m., steady on flow and stage against 93.8 cfs and 1.6 feet in the fetcher's 24-hour comparison.
waters.working: The gauge at Dyer reads 97.3 cfs and steady, about 5 cfs over the 92.1 that Tuesday's paper carried at the same hour and still inside the late-autumn base flow the river has settled into since the weekend bump ran off. At 97 cfs and clear it is a long-leader, small-fly problem, with the fish on the pocket-water lies and the tailouts rather than the seams, and after another cold night the midday hours fish best once the sun is on the water. A size 18 to 20 midge or a small Blue-winged Olive nymph under a soft indicator on a long leader through the slower pockets and the tailouts is the pattern, a stonefly nymph as the point fly in the deeper plunge pools where the larger fish hold in cold water, and a sculpin pattern swung tight to the undercut banks in the first and last hour of light.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.79 feet at 5 a.m., falling against 25.05 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.8 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool with ordinary bank access, down about a quarter of a foot in 24 hours and 18 hundredths under Tuesday's printed reading. The wing dams and the riprap are showing rock and the water is clear enough to fish structure rather than the slack behind it: shad are the forage, so a white or shad-pattern swimbait or a lipless crankbait worked down the face of the wing dams and along the riprap is the pattern, slowed down for water that saw frost inland again overnight, with a jig and crawfish on the slack side of the lock wall for the fish holding off the current. The R.C. Byrd tailwater itself is not gauged; this is the pool side.
waters.source: USGS 03201500 (Ohio River at Point Pleasant); config.SPORTSMAN_WATERS

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.45 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 26.62 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.4 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool and steady, 45 hundredths over the 26.0 feet Tuesday's paper carried, so the lower gauge has taken back some of what it gave up between Monday and Tuesday while the upper gauge falls. Below the dam the pattern is the structure the dam makes: skipjack and shad stack in the current below the gates, and a spoon or a heavy jig worked in the churn, or a live skipjack drifted along the current seams off the lock wall, is the hybrid and catfish setup; the riprap along the Huntington bank fishes a crawfish-colour jig on the slack side where the bank current breaks. Huntington is the downstream bracket, 30-odd river miles below the dam, not the tailwater reading, which the Corps publish and this pipeline cannot fetch.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: high 2:12 AM at 3.1 ft, low 8:35 AM at 0.8 ft, high 2:35 PM at 3.5 ft, low 9:11 PM at 0.6 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 1:29 AM at 3.6 ft, low 7:23 AM at 1.1 ft, high 1:43 PM at 4.1 ft, low 8:03 PM at 0.8 ft. Water 56.8F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:36 a.m. Moon waxing gibbous, 62% illuminated, 8.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 2:12 AM and 2:35 PM in the sound.
waters.working: All eight events land inside Wednesday on both stations again, the table about 50 minutes later than Tuesday's. The sound lags the surf by 43 minutes on the overnight high, 72 on the morning low, 52 on the afternoon high and 68 on the evening low, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills; the afternoon flood climbs 2.7 feet from the 8:35 low to the 2:35 high and the evening ebb drops 2.9 feet to the 9:11 low, and at waxing gibbous and 62% the moon is a day and a half past the quarter, so the current through the inlet is building toward the full moon from the neap. The water at Beaufort read 56.8F at 5:36 a.m., down 1.3 degrees from Tuesday's reading after a fourth cold night. The NWS alerts feed for North Carolina, read at 5:47 a.m., carried no active product for the coast: no frost advisory, rip current or beach hazards statement. The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report, a monthly, is dated Nov. 1 and is 17 days old, so it is the month's pattern and not this morning's conditions: East Coast Sports reports the piers taking a few big red drum of 32 inches and up on the north end, a mix of smaller red drum and the occasional speckled trout in the sound with the focus shifting to almost exclusive trout action as the weather cools; Native Son says the deeper seams of 5 to 8 feet in the main creeks are the trout target and cut bait the best bet for scattered reds; Speckled Specialist reports live shrimp under a cork in 4 to 16 feet of water and 3/16-ounce jig heads with a soft plastic for artificials; Jolly Roger Pier reports scattered speckled trout, Virginia mullet and spot at night and thick bluefish early. Tied to today's table and a sound in the mid 50s, the 8:35 low falls in the cold and the window is the top of the flood and the first of the ebb, roughly 1:15 to 4:15 p.m., once the sun has been on the flats: trout in the 5-to-8-foot creek-channel seams and along the ICWW channel edge on a 3/16-ounce jig head and a small soft plastic worked slowly, or a live shrimp under a popping cork drifted over the oyster bars at the creek mouths as the water starts to leave the grass. Red drum want the last of the fall, roughly 6:15 to the 9:11 p.m. low, which runs well into dark, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges, or a soft plastic on the oyster and grass banks in the last of the light; the flooded-grass window for a weedless gold spoon is the hour before the 2:35 high. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel on the last of the flood; bluefish are the beach fish on a metal jig in the early morning. Flounder are release only.
